content: 1. Tramadol affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor patients closely when administering this drug. 2. Trazodone and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. This combination is serious; consider using an alternative therapy. 3. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Triclabendazole and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Triclabendazole also increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor plasma concentrations during and after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 7. Trifluoperazine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Trimethoprim and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Trimipramine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 11. Tropisetron and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. 13. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 16. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when coadministering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 17. Voriconazole increases the toxicity of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%; reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 18. Voriconazole increases the levels of vinblastine by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 20. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 21. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 22. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as either drug can increase the toxicity of the other through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Vorinostat and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 27. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 28. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 29. Voriconazole and ziprasidone both increase the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 30. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 31. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 32. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the zuranolone dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Voriconazole is associated with visual changes, including photophobia, color changes, increased or decreased visual acuity, and blurred vision, occurring in 21% of patients. 34. Cardiovascular effects include tachycardia, hypertension, hypotension, vasodilation, and peripheral edema. 35. Other adverse effects include fever, chills, headache, hallucinations, dizziness, rash, pruritus, photosensitizing skin reactions, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, xerostomia, thrombocytopenia, increased alkaline phosphatase, increased serum transaminases (ALT/AST), cholestatic jaundice, and acute renal failure. 36. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs), such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), have been reported. Discontinue therapy if these occur. 37. Voriconazole therapy is associated with QT interval prolongation. Exercise caution in patients with proarrhythmic conditions, such as congenital or acquired QT prolongation, sinus bradycardia, symptomatic arrhythmias, or cardiomyopathy, especially if heart failure is present. Correct potassium, magnesium, and calcium levels before initiating therapy. 38. Voriconazole is contraindicated in patients with hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. 39. Voriconazole is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless the benefits outweigh the risks to the fetus. Inform patients of potential hazards. 40. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment. 41. There is no data on the presence of voriconazole in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production. Weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother’s clinical need for therapy and potential adverse effects on the child. 42. Voriconazole therapy has no activity against Zygomycetes and may increase the incidence of zygomycosis. 43. Long-term treatment with voriconazole has been associated with fluorosis and periostitis. Discontinue therapy if these occur. 44. Monitor patients with risk factors for acute pancreatitis (e.g., recent chemotherapy, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation) for symptoms of pancreatitis during therapy. 45. Voriconazole therapy can cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women. There are no adequate data on its use in pregnancy. 46. Reconstitute voriconazole with 19 mL of sterile water for injection to obtain a 10 mg/mL solution. Shake until fully dissolved. The reconstituted product can be further diluted for infusion in various solutions, such as normal saline, lactated Ringer’s, or dextrose-containing solutions. 47. Voriconazole has a bioavailability of 96%, is metabolized via hepatic CYP2C19, CYP2C9, and CYP3A4, and is excreted primarily in the urine (80%). Protein binding is approximately 58%.
